slots.brief: Two masses on a rod; find where the centre of mass lies from one end.
Given galvanometer resistance and full-scale deflection current, find the multiplier resistance to convert it to a voltmeter of a given range.
Three coplanar forces acting at a point; use equilibrium conditions to find the magnitude of one force.
Given the momentum of a body, find its kinetic energy (or use KE–p relation to compare two bodies).
A diode in series with resistors across a battery; assuming a constant forward voltage drop, find the circuit current.
A bridge with four resistors; identify the condition for balance and find the unknown resistance for zero galvanometer deflection.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated particles
slots.brief: Compare the de Broglie wavelengths of two particles accelerated through the same potential difference.
Compare a given trajectory equation y = ax – bx² with the standard form to extract the angle of projection.
A rectangular cycle on a P–V diagram; find the net work done from the enclosed area.
A Zener regulator with a series resistance and varying input voltage; find the current through the Zener when the load draws a given current.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.brief: Conceptual question on how stopping potential and photocurrent change when intensity/frequency of incident light is varied.
Given the rms electric field of an EM wave, compute the average energy density using u = ε₀E².
Find the energy (or wavelength) of the photon emitted when an electron in a hydrogen-like ion jumps from n=2 to n=1.
A wire is stretched to double its length at constant volume; find the factor by which resistance changes.

slots.subtopic: Field of a dipole on equatorial line
slots.brief: Given dipole moment, find the electric field magnitude at a point on the equatorial line at a given distance.
Given the masses of a nucleus and its constituents, compute the binding energy of the nucleus.
Find the dimensional formula of a given physical quantity (e.g., torque, Planck's constant, coefficient of viscosity) from its defining equation.
From a given wave equation y = A sin(kx − ωt + φ), read off the amplitude, frequency, wavelength and wave speed.
Use T² ∝ a³ to find the orbital period (or semi-major axis) of a planet compared to that of Earth.
Using a symmetric Gaussian surface to find the field outside a uniformly charged sphere and explain why the field inside a shell is zero.
Given the phase difference between two waves at a point on the screen, find the resultant intensity as a fraction of the maximum.
Given magnetic flux through a coil varying with time as a polynomial, use Faraday's law to find the induced emf at a given instant.
Compare rms speeds of two gases at the same temperature using v ∝ 1/√M.
For a body rolling without slipping, relate the velocity of a point on the rim (e.g., topmost or contact point) to the centre-of-mass velocity.
Given the temperature of a gas, compute the average translational kinetic energy per molecule using (3/2)kT.
Given a diagram showing a compass/inclination at a place, use the dip angle relation to find the horizontal or vertical component of Earth's field.
A body cools from one temperature to another in a given time; use Newton's law of cooling to find the time for a further drop in temperature.
Given the focal lengths of objective and eyepiece, find the magnifying power and tube length of an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment.
A source moving toward then away from a stationary observer; compare the observed frequencies in the two cases.
Statement-based question on Huygens' principle: construction of wavefronts and what each point on a wavefront represents.
Two wires of the same material but different lengths and radii under the same load; compare their elongations using Y = (F/A)(L/ΔL).
Given R, X_L and X_C, compute the impedance and the phase angle between the current and the source voltage.

slots.subtopic: Magnetic field due to finite wire / polygon loop
slots.brief: Find B at the centre of a regular polygon of wire carrying current, using superposition of the finite-segment formula.
Ice at 0°C mixed with water at a higher temperature; use latent heat plus specific heat to find the final temperature (or remaining ice).
Find the minimum launch speed (or energy needed) for a body to escape from a planet's surface using energy conservation.
Two blocks connected by a rope on a frictionless table (or an incline); write free-body equations and find the common acceleration and rope tension.
Given the terminal velocity of a sphere of one radius, find the terminal velocity of a sphere of a different radius in the same fluid.
A mixed series–parallel capacitor network connected to batteries; find the equivalent capacitance and charge on a specified capacitor.
Two springs in series (or parallel); find the equivalent spring constant and the resulting time period of an attached mass.
Given r(t), differentiate to find the velocity vector and its magnitude at a given time.
Four PQRS parts of a short factual paragraph (e.g., about a daily habit or simple scientific fact) to be ordered; one part clearly opens with a general statement and another closes with a conclusion.
Simple sentence where the verb disagrees with its subject (e.g., 'The list of items are...'); student picks the erroneous part, with 'no error' not among options.
Four short jumbled sentences with a simple narrative flow (e.g., waking up, an event, its result); ask which sentence logically comes first.
Ask for the closest meaning of a moderately common word like 'candid' or 'diligent' used in a neutral context sentence.
Sentence misusing a preposition or requiring a gerund after a preposition (e.g., 'insisted on going' pattern); pick the corrected version of the underlined part.
Ask the figurative meaning of a less common idiom such as 'to bell the cat' or 'a wild goose chase' given in a short context sentence; distractors should be literal meanings.
Sentence with a tense inconsistency across clauses (e.g., past event described with present perfect later); identify the incorrect part.
Easy single-blank sentence where context clearly points to a common word (e.g., 'The teacher praised her for her ___ in completing the project' - diligence).
Ask for the opposite of a simple, high-frequency word like 'abundant' or 'transparent'.
Sentence with a time clause requiring the correct tense (e.g., 'By the time we arrived, the show ___ started' - present perfect vs past perfect choice).
Moderate analogy pair (e.g., 'Cure : Doctor :: Repair : Mechanic' or 'Chapter : Book :: Scene : Play'); student picks the matching pair from options.
Identify the correctly spelled word among four misspellings of a commonly misspelled word like 'accommodate' or 'occurrence'.
Ask the meaning of a straightforward word like 'generous' or 'brave' given in a short sentence.
Give a pair like 'AC : 3' where the code is derived from positional values of letters; candidate must apply the same rule to find the missing code for a new letter pair.
Two statements (e.g., all A are B, some B are C) with four conclusion options including a 'possibility' conclusion; ask which conclusions follow.
A simple word is coded by shifting each letter forward by a fixed number; give the code for one word and ask for the code of another using the same shift.
A series mixing letters and digits following a simple pattern (e.g., letter shifts +1, digit increases by 2); find the next term.
Four words where three share a common category/property and one differs; ask which one does not belong (keep distinction clear-cut, e.g., three are herbivores and one is not).
Give four words with subtle first-letter/second-letter differences; ask which word comes first (or third) as per dictionary order.

Describe a small family (e.g., a couple with children and their spouses) and ask how many members of a specific type exist, such as number of males or females, given one ambiguous member described by role.
Give a two-parameter family of curves (e.g. y = Ae^{2x} + B e^{-3x}) and ask students to form the differential equation by eliminating the arbitrary constants.

Ask for the intervals where a cubic-based function with a parameter is increasing/decreasing, requiring analysis of derivative sign and a condition on the parameter for a given interval of monotonicity.
Use the identity a×(b×c) = (a·c)b − (a·b)c to compute a vector expression for given simple vectors; ask for the resulting vector or its magnitude.
Solve an equation reducible to a quadratic in sin x (e.g. via double-angle substitution) and express the general solution as a set.
Evaluate a definite integral over [−a, a] whose integrand splits into an odd part (drops) plus a simple even part, using symmetry and a standard result.
Give a 3×3 system with a parameter λ; find the value(s) of λ for which the system has infinitely many solutions and check Δx = Δy = Δz = 0 for those values.
Give a small set of 5–6 observations (small integers, mean an integer) and ask for the variance or standard deviation directly by computation.
Find the natural domain of a function combining a square root and a logarithm (or rational expression), obtained by intersecting the conditions from each part.
A related-rates problem, e.g. water draining from a conical vessel or a ladder sliding, requiring differentiation of a volume/geometric relation at an instant; ask for the required rate.

slots.subtopic: Range of a sin + b cos
slots.brief: Find the range (or max/min value) of an expression of the form a sin θ + b cos θ + c, possibly with a constraint on θ, using the amplitude bound.
A straightforward indefinite integral solved by a single substitution such as u = x² + 1 or a trigonometric substitution; ask for the antiderivative.
Given the equation of an ellipse in shifted/non-standard form, find its eccentricity (or foci) using b² = a²(1 − e²) after reading off a and b.
Find the equation of the circle passing through three given points (or through two points with a stated condition) by solving for centre and radius.
Arrange letters of a word or people in a row with restrictions such as vowels together and/or two particular items never adjacent; ask for the number of arrangements (complement counting optional).
A binomial experiment (e.g. coins/dice/defective items) with small n; ask for the probability of exactly k successes or at least one success using the binomial formula.
Find the coefficient of a specific power of x in the expansion of (a + bxⁿ)^k by writing the general term and matching exponents.
Given z in a form requiring algebraic manipulation (e.g. (1+i)/(1−i) raised to a power), find the modulus and principal argument of the result.
Count the number of onto (surjective) functions from a set of m elements to a set of n elements using the inclusion–exclusion formula; small numbers.
Two lines given in symmetric form with a parameter; determine the value of the parameter for which the lines intersect (using the coplanarity/shortest-distance determinant condition).
Find the equation of the line through the intersection point of two given lines and passing through an external point, using the family L1 + λL2 = 0.
Given two direction cosines (or a ratio condition), find the third using l² + m² + n² = 1, with attention to sign.
Evaluate a definite integral of a trigonometric integrand (e.g. sin³x cos²x type or using a standard reduction), possibly using symmetry over a symmetric limit.
Find the equation of the tangent (or normal) to a curve at a given point, e.g. y² = 4ax or a hyperbola; ask for the line or its intercepts.
Find the range of a rational function f(x) = (linear)/(quadratic) by setting y = f(x) and demanding real x (discriminant ≥ 0).
Given a GP with |r| < 1 and a simple relation between two partial sums (e.g. S∞ = 4·S2), find the first term or the common ratio, then a requested sum.
Given cardinalities of A, B and their union/intersection, compute |A ∪ B| or |A − B|; or verify a stated set identity with small concrete sets.
Solve a rational inequality of the form (x − a)(x − b)/((x − c)(x + d)) ≤ 0 using the wavy-curve method; give the solution set.
Evaluate an indefinite integral of the form ∫ (polynomial)·(exponential or inverse-trig or log) dx requiring integration by parts, possibly applied twice.
Use differentials to approximate a value such as √(a + small change) or (a + h)^{1/n}, asking for the approximate value or the percentage error.
Compute the box product [a b c] for given position-type vectors, or use it to find the volume of a parallelepiped/condition for coplanarity; vectors chosen so components are small integers.
Evaluate an expression like tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y or a composite sin⁻¹(something) reduced via standard identities, with a branch/sign subtlety; small numbers.
Count the number of n-digit numbers formed from a given digit multiset satisfying a condition such as divisibility by 5 or digits in increasing order; split into cases.
A standard Bayes setup: e.g. three machines/factories with known defect rates and output fractions; find the (posterior) probability that a defective item came from a given source.
Given a matrix equation A² = A or A² = I (or a specific 2×2 matrix), compute a higher power like Aⁿ or an expression like A⁵ from the pattern; small n with pattern recognition.
Give a compound statement involving ∧, ∨ and negation and ask which of the given options is logically equivalent to it (using De Morgan's laws or truth-table reasoning).
Find the distance between two parallel lines (or between a point and a line) in a form requiring rewriting into ax + by + c = 0; direct formula application.
Given a quadratic with roots α, β and one root satisfying an extra condition (or given α + β and αβ), find the value of a requested symmetric expression or an unknown coefficient.
Evaluate a limit of the form sin(kx)/tan(mx) or (1 − cos kx)/x² using standard trigonometric limits; small coefficient manipulation.
Evaluate (or show) a determinant whose rows/columns have entries built from sums, using row operations C1 → C1 + C2 + C3 to factor the determinant into a product.
Find the area enclosed between a parabola and a line (or two curves) that intersect at two points; requires setting up the correct definite integral with the right ordering of curves.
Solve a linear ODE dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) with a simple integrating factor (e.g. P = 1/x or 2/x type), and find the particular solution through a given point.
Find the condition on k for a line y = mx + c to be tangent to a circle (or for two circles to touch), using distance from centre = radius; then a numerical value.
Use the 3D distance formula: e.g. verify collinearity of three points in space or find a point on an axis equidistant from two given points.
Interpret |z − z₁| = k|z − z₂| as a circle (Apollonius) or find the locus of z; ask for the centre/radius of the locus or the maximum modulus on a segment.
Evaluate a limit of the form (1 + a/x)^{bx} or (a^x − b^x)/x reduced to the e-limb standard form; require algebraic rewriting before applying the standard limit.
